supersedes: capability-preflight.v1.json (a4d8a02) - v1 is kept as historical record, not deleted
supersedeReason: v1 conflated OpenRouter's supported_parameters CAPABILITY LABEL ('structured_outputs') with the actual WIRE FIELD NAME a request must send ('response_format'). OpenRouter's own model catalog and Structured Outputs documentation describe 'structured_outputs' as a filterable capability identifier (e.g. supported_parameters=structured_outputs finds models that accept response_format.type=json_schema); the request itself is always sent as response_format regardless of which capability label the catalog uses to describe support for it. v1's inference - 'response_format absent from supported_parameters therefore the endpoint rejects the response_format field' - does not follow from that semantics and is withdrawn.

correctedCapabilityReading.responseFormatWireField: ELIGIBLE_FOR_PREFLIGHT - the correct request shape per OpenRouter's Structured Outputs guide is response_format: { type: "json_schema", json_schema: { name, strict: true, schema } }, sent regardless of the capability-label naming quirk
correctedCapabilityReading.strictJsonSchemaAcceptance: UNVERIFIED_UNTIL_REQUEST_ACCEPTED - metadata confirms the capability LABEL, not which JSON-Schema keyword subset ModelRun's backend actually honors (oneOf, additionalProperties:false, enum, nested required, etc.). This is not re-litigated as blocked; it is carried forward as an explicit unverified flag through preflight and only resolved by whether the real request is accepted once authorized.
correctedCapabilityReading.streamAndUsageInclude: not distinguishable from supported_parameters alone; carried as unverified the same way
correctedCapabilityReading.reasoningNone: supported_parameters lists reasoning/reasoning_effort/include_reasoning; reasoning={effort:"none"} is the same shape already used for qwen3.7-flash and is expected to work
correctedCapabilityReading.requireParametersTrueAllowFallbacksFalse: compatible with routing: exactly one provider (ModelRun) serves this slug, so require_parameters=true has nothing else to fall back past, and allow_fallbacks=false is a no-op safety net rather than a live constraint

note: This correction itself makes no provider call. The strict-schema acceptance question is answered empirically only once a separate, explicit authorization opens the 3-call gate (V5CanaryGate) after the preflight below is frozen - not by this file.
